final_narrative:
The enrichment analysis clearly points to **Eicosanoid synthesis (WikiPathways WP167)** as the dominant affected pathway, with five of the seven input metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — all belonging to this pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment ≈ 1429.7). Membership verification confirms that arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 5-HETE (C04805) are all annotated in this pathway.

KEGG reaction graph analysis establishes directional flow from arachidonic acid (C00219) toward both 5-HETE and Leukotriene A4 through a shared intermediate, placing arachidonic acid definitively upstream. The presence of 15-HETE alongside the 5-lipoxygenase product 5-HETE within the same pathway suggests coordinated dysregulation of both the 12-lipoxygenase and 5-lipoxygenase branches of the eicosanoid cascade. 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) represents the cyclopentenone prostaglandin arm derived from PGD2 metabolism. Losartan (C07072) belongs to the Losartan Action Pathway (SMPDB) and glycolaldehyde (C00266) belongs to Vitamin B6 Metabolism (KEGG) — neither is part of the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway.

The biological significance centers on **lipid mediator storm**: elevated HETEs and Leukotriene A4 indicate heightened phospholipase A2 activity releasing arachidonic acid, followed by amplified 5-LOX and 12-LOX activity. This pattern is consistent with inflammatory activation, where eicosanoids drive leukocyte chemotaxis and vasoconstriction. 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 adds a PPARγ-activating, anti-inflammatory nuance. Together, these shifts implicate an inflammatory response in the treatment group.
